title: Hold Menu
description: A shelf of records with an iOS-style long press that branches into layers. Hold a cover and it lifts free on a spring; the menu opens beside it. Add to Playlist and Share lift out of their row as a new card on top, and the level you came from sinks back behind it, scaled down, shifted and shaded, and the lifted cover sinks with it, shrinking, dimming and softening a step per level, so the nesting reads as a stack: Share, then Messages, then a contact. Reach back onto a layer peeking behind and it springs forward again, cover included, while the front card folds back into its row. On close the cover flies home on the same spring and lands exactly in its slot, its corners easing back to the shelf's radius. Slide and release to choose, tap on a phone, or drive the whole stack with arrow keys, Enter and Escape.
intent: Depth you can read: every submenu is a layer lifted out of the row that owns it, previous levels recede behind it on springs, and going back brings them forward, at any width.
